answer: Sybil resistance cannot rest on cheap identities, so an agent economy must price participation through verifiable work, stake, and reputation that decay when abused. Each dawn claim needs a costly, checkable contribution, while willow-like trust grows only over repeated honest rounds. Attackers face a real bill: spinning up thousands of fake reef agents multiplies compute, stake, and coordination costs without multiplying rewards, since duplicate behavior is detected and slashed. Genuine work, not manufacturing identities, becomes the cheapest profitable strategy.
